item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 31, 2026
item.description:
A Bentonville-based real estate company has donated 33 acres known as the John Rich Homestead to the city of Pea Ridge.
Pea Ridge receives 33-acre John Rich Homestead donation. A Bentonville-based real estate company related to the Walton family has donated 33 acres known as the John Rich Homestead to the city of Pea Ridge.
On the Bentonville Library Advisory Board agenda: Public comments on agenda items. Residents can speak for up to 3 minutes on items on the agenda by registering with their name, address, phone number, and email address.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates from the city of Bentonville on airport operations and events. This includes information on airport webpage upgrades, upcoming events like the Game Aerospace & Bell Helicopter Event, the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, fuel tank cleaning, the Snow and Ice Management Plan, Eastside Hangar Development, crane operations near I-49 S, and the 2026 Budget.
Siloam Springs City Hall repairs expected to conclude by year's end. Siloam Springs City Hall, closed since the beginning of the year due to water damage, is set to complete repairs and reopen to the public by the end of the year.
Pearlsnap Picnic opens cafe in Jones Center. Pearlsnap Picnic, an approximately 2,500-square-foot coffee and smoothie bar, recently opened in the Jones Center in Springdale.
Pea Ridge Police issue statement on electric bike usage. The Pea Ridge Police Department released a statement regarding the use of electric bikes and similar devices in the city, prompted by numerous complaints and social media posts.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Audit recommends changes for Benton County court case assignments. An audit of Benton County court case assignments recommends the state Administrative Office of the Courts consider requiring documentation for all case transfers and electronic sign-off by a second authorized person.
Springdale Chamber of Commerce hires director of economic development. The Springdale Chamber of Commerce has announced new hires, including a director of economic development.
Jurassic Quest brings dinosaurs to Rogers Convention Center. Jurassic Quest brought hundreds of life-size dinosaurs, including a T. rex and Spinosaurus, to the Rogers Convention Center.
Rogers hosts Family Fun Day with free activities. Families in Rogers enjoyed an afternoon of free activities, food, music, and community at Family Fun Day on Sunday, August 30.
Lawnly to debut Lawn Care Olympics in Fayetteville on September 20. Lawnly, a tech platform for lawn care, will debut the first-ever Lawn Care Olympics in Fayetteville on September 20.
Arkansas Nepali community aids Nepal flood victims. Members of the Northwest Arkansas Nepali community gathered to support people affected by disasters in Nepal.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 30, 2026
item.description:
The Little Sugar MTB race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Walmart implements new technology in stores. Walmart has been implementing new technology in its stores, including drone delivery, the "Auto Care Center of the Future," and digital shelf labels.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 29, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville and Springdale hospitals have been designated as Level III trauma centers by the Arkansas Department of Health.
Bentonville and Springdale hospitals become Level III trauma centers. Freeman Health System hospitals in Bentonville and Springdale received Level III trauma center designations from the Arkansas Department of Health.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026.
Boutique hotel in Rogers to open in September. A boutique hotel in Rogers is scheduled to open in September.
Fayetteville school board to consider renaming space. The Fayetteville School Board will consider renaming the Fayetteville High School performing arts center after a longtime theater instructor.
Jones center hosts 'Every child swims' program. The Jones Center is hosting the 'Every Child Swims' program for elementary students from multiple Springdale schools.
Fayetteville artist completes trail art at Gregory Park. Fayetteville artist Jason Jones completed three interactive artworks on mountain bike trails at Gregory Park in Fayetteville, a project that cost $11,600 over eight years.
Gentry blacksmith forges knives and swords. Wayne Johnson, a blacksmith in Gentry, has built Valhalla Forging since 2018, creating items such as knives, swords, and hair pins.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 28, 2026
item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court continued its consideration of an ordinance to establish a fund for the 287(g) program.
Benton County Quorum Court continues 287(g) fund consideration. The Benton County Quorum Court continued its consideration of an ordinance to establish an account for funds generated through the 287(g) program. Dozens of people gathered at the meeting to discuss the matter.
Benton County Quorum Court hears public pushback on ICE partnership. The Benton County Quorum Court heard comments regarding the county's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at its Thursday meeting.
Fayetteville School Board approves maximum price for new Ramay junior high. The Fayetteville School Board approved the guaranteed maximum price for the construction of the new Ramay Junior High School, set at just under $117 million.
Fayetteville School Board approves price for new Ramay junior high site. The Fayetteville School Board voted to approve the guaranteed maximum price for the construction of the new Ramay Junior High School.
American Airlines adds new one-stop flights from XNA to europe in 2027. American Airlines announced it will add new one-stop flights from Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) to several European destinations in 2027.
Work continues on Fayetteville competition stadium remodel. Work is continuing on the remodel of the competition stadium in Fayetteville, which will be the future home turf for the Fayetteville School District's junior high teams.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Former Tyson Foods executive named CFO at Hormel Foods. A former Tyson Foods executive has been named the chief financial officer at Hormel Foods.
Bentonville girls golf team wins fort smith tournament. The Bentonville girls golf team won the Fort Smith tournament.
Bentonville tennis prevails over Rogers squad. The Bentonville tennis team prevailed over Rogers in a match between two top teams in the 6A-West Conference at Memorial Park.
Japanese artist behind Crystal Bridges 'Infinity mirrored Room' dies at 97. Yayoi Kusama, the artist behind the Infinity Room at the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, has died at 97.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 27, 2026
item.description:
Southwest D Street in Bentonville will close until October 2 for infrastructure work.
Southwest D Street in Bentonville to close through October 2. Southwest D Street between Southwest 20th Street and Southwest 24th Street will be closed for infrastructure work until October 2.
Bentonville City Council approves morning star schoolhouse property donation. The Bentonville City Council approved the donation of the Morning Star Schoolhouse property, which the Parks and Recreation Department plans to revitalize.
Bentonville City Council amends noise regulations. The Bentonville City Council approved amendments to a city ordinance concerning noise regulations following complaints from businesses and residents.
Triton Ventures opens headquarters in Bentonville. Bentonville AI startup Triton Ventures opened its new headquarters at North ROC, an office and coworking campus.
Scott Family Amazeum to open expansion this fall. The Scott Family Amazeum in Bentonville will open approximately 34,740 square feet of new indoor and outdoor space this fall, adjacent to its existing 50,000-square-foot museum.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Pasture in Lowell sells for $4.3 million. More than 12 acres of pasture along Interstate 49 in Lowell recently sold for $4.33 million, equating to $348,479 per acre.
August sales tax revenue falls in Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale. Sales tax revenue reported in August for Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale totaled $10.001 million, a 0.12% decrease from the same month last year.
Walton children to be inducted into business hall of fame. Rob Walton, Alice Walton, Jim Walton, and the late John Walton, children of Walmart founders Sam and Helen Walton, will be inducted into the Arkansas Business Hall of Fame.
Rogers City Council meeting cancelled. The Rogers City Council meeting scheduled for September 8, 2026, has been cancelled.
Rogers fire Pension and Relief Board to meet. The Fire Pension and Relief Board will hold a meeting from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at 301 W. Chestnut Street in Rogers.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 26, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville City Council approved amendments to noise regulations, setting new decibel limits and times for music.
Bentonville City Council approves noise regulation amendments. Bentonville City Council approved amendments to noise regulations, which will set specific decibel levels and times for music starting next month.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport board approves construction contract for new concourse. The Northwest Arkansas National Airport board approved a construction contract for a new western concourse and other amenities. The $78.78 million project will add a two-level, approximately 111,000-square-foot expansion on the west side of the terminal.
Rogers City Council approves $3.9 million in federal grant money for street projects. The Rogers City Council approved the acceptance of more than $3 million in federal money for street and road improvements.
Healthcare startups to participate in Northwest Arkansas pilot program. Healthcare startups in Northwest Arkansas have been selected by Arkansas-based healthtech accelerator HTA and startup-connection organization NXTUS Inc. for $20,000 Community Pilot Projects.
Walmart, tyson foods, and autonomous trucking partner announce $200 million in funding. Gatik AI Inc., an autonomous trucking provider with customers including Walmart and Tyson Foods, announced it raised $200 million in a new funding series.
Collier & Associates enters deal to use Compass International technology. Fayetteville-based real estate company Collier & Associates established a private-label partnership with Compass International Holdings, a New York-based real estate services company.
UAMS and NWACC announce partnership to support student athletes. The Northwest Arkansas Community College and University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences signed a memorandum of understanding for UAMS Health to provide annual screening and injury prevention support to NWACC athletes.
University of Arkansas calls off plans for walk-thru 7 brew on campus. The University of Arkansas has called off plans for a new 7 Brew location to open on campus this fall.
Centerton unveils downtown revitalization plan. The City of Centerton unveiled its downtown revitalization plan at a recent City Council meeting.
Thaden School in Bentonville opens new gymnasium. Thaden School in Bentonville cut the ribbon for its new gymnasium.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 25, 2026
item.description:
The Centerton Planning Commission will consider a final draft of the city's downtown master plan on September 1.
Rogers to have overnight lane closures on West walnut street. Overnight lane closures are scheduled for West Walnut Street in Rogers for a couple of weeks due to a road resurfacing project.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to approve waiving competitive bidding for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the city's electric utility to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Council to accept $2,372,920.00 in grant funds for Greenhouse Road improvements. This would provide funding for right-of-way and utility activities related to the Greenhouse Road Improvements project.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Public hearing on declaring a nuisance structure at 820 w. Rife Circle. Residents can provide input on whether the structure at 820 W. Rife Circle should be declared a nuisance and ordered to be razed and removed.
Madison county approves three-year data center ban. Madison County approved a three-year moratorium on data center development, joining other counties in the state with similar restrictions.
Two Rogers churches consider land for affordable housing. Two churches in Rogers are considering using their land for affordable housing. Faith organizations in Benton and Washington counties own over 7 square miles of land, with nearly half of it vacant.
Walmart NW Arkansas Championship marks 20th year. The Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship presented by P&G is celebrating its 20th year. A preview event was held with panels discussing the golf tournament's impact.
UAMS Health partners with NWACC for student-athlete care. UAMS Health and NorthWest Arkansas Community College (NWACC) have partnered to allow UAMS Health students to provide pre-participation physical examinations and injury-assessment screenings for NWACC student-athletes.
Arkansas' longest-running marathon ends. After 50 years, the Hogeye marathon and relays in Northwest Arkansas are being discontinued.
Experience Fayetteville and University of Arkansas to offer new gameday experience. Experience Fayetteville and the University of Arkansas are collaborating to introduce a new gameday experience, including a parade to Razorback Stadium. Fans can also participate in a 'Trailgating' experience connecting downtown and the stadium.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Walmart and other businesses raise concerns over Entergy rate increase. Walmart and a group representing Arkansas' hospitals, colleges, and universities have expressed concerns about Entergy Arkansas' rate case, which is currently before the Public Service Commission.
Walton Arts Center hosts Halloween costume drive. The Walton Arts Center is hosting a Halloween costume donation drive for elementary students as part of Welcoming Week NWA.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 24, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville's City Council will consider a resolution to approve a $700,000 grant for a traffic signal at SW Regional Airport Boulevard and SW I Street.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to approve waiving competitive bidding for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the Bentonville Electric Utility Department (BEUD) to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, due to market volatility and lead times.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Council to accept a $2,372,920.00 grant for Greenhouse Road improvements. This would provide funding for right-of-way and utility activities related to the Greenhouse Road Improvements project.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent, as outlined in Ordinance No. 2017-15.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to hold a public hearing on declaring a nuisance structure at 820 w. Rife Circle. Residents can provide input on whether a structure at 820 W. Rife Circle should be declared a nuisance and ordered to be razed and removed.
Siloam Springs School District accepts $925,000 offer for Kenwood Road property. The Siloam Springs School District accepted a $925,000 offer for approximately 25 acres off East Kenwood Road, which will contribute to the DaySpring building remodel.
Hogeye Marathon will not continue in 2027. The Hogeye Marathon will not continue in 2027, with organizers planning to focus on shorter races.
Bentonville couple launch direct-to-consumer denim brand. A Bentonville couple, Anastasia and Stefan de Jong, launched a direct-to-consumer denim brand.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Gentry mayor plans to retire at year-end. Gentry's mayor plans to retire after this year, leaving the position's future unclear.
Arkansas Music Week returns to Fayetteville August 23-30. Arkansas Music Week will return to Fayetteville from August 23-30 for a week-long celebration of local music, culture, and creativity.
Housing policy runs through Arkansas. Arkansas communities face various housing pressures, with Northwest Arkansas working to keep pace with growth and rural areas struggling to attract builders.
ICE fears impact Northwest Arkansas festivals. Immigrant rights advocates state that fears and backlash related to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement have contributed to lower attendance at Northwest Arkansas festivals.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 23, 2026
item.description:
Bella Vista's renovated City Hall will open on Wednesday, August 26.
Bella Vista City Hall to open after renovation. The renovated Bella Vista City Hall will officially open on Wednesday, August 26.
Benton County experiences widespread power outage. More than 15,000 Carroll Electric customers in Benton County lost power on Saturday afternoon.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Committee to approve waiving bids for electrical breakers for BEUD substations. This would allow Bentonville Electric Utility Department (BEUD) to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax without competitive bidding, due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 301 SE B Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family, to T3.2, Neighborhood Transition. This change in zoning classification for the property at 301 SE B Street could allow for different types of development than currently permitted for suburban single-family homes.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This change would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to accept a federal grant for safe streets and amend the 2026 budget. This would allow the city to receive a federal grant of up to $3,987,536.00 from the U.S. Department of Transportation for safe streets initiatives and appropriate $4,984,420.00 for related expenses.
Dodo coffee to open new flagship store in Fayetteville. A Fayetteville coffee shop, Dodo Coffee, is preparing to open its new flagship location.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
100 Black Men of Northwest Arkansas holds informational meeting. The 100 Black Men of Northwest Arkansas held a membership informational meeting at the Fayetteville Public Library for community members interested in the organization.
Northwest Arkansas business briefs include Arvest Bank recognition. Northwest Arkansas business news includes Arvest Bank being recognized on Forbes' list of best employers.
Local cross country season begins this week. The 2026 cross country season is set to begin statewide this week, with Northwest Arkansas' first race, the Shiloh Saints Invitational, scheduled for Saturday.
Fayetteville volleyball team looks to contend for state championship. The Fayetteville Lady Purple Bulldogs, under new leadership, are expected to be contenders for the state volleyball championship after finishing as runner-up last year.
Elkins elks expect to repeat as champions. The Elkins Elks expect to repeat as Class 4A state champions, despite being picked second in 4A-1 behind Gravette.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 22, 2026
item.description:
A portion of Northwest A Street in Bentonville will close Monday for water main repairs.
Bentonville closes Northwest A Street for water main repair. A section of Northwest A Street between Northwest Ninth and Northwest Park streets in Bentonville will be closed from 9 a.m. Monday to 2 a.m. Tuesday for water main repairs.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Council to consider waiving competitive bidding for electrical equipment purchase. This would allow Bentonville Electric Utility Department (BEUD) to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, which are needed for future substation projects.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone property at 301 SE B Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family, to T3.2, Neighborhood Transition. This change in zoning classification could allow for different types of development or density on the property at 301 SE B Street than currently permitted for suburban single-family homes.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This change would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to accept a federal grant for safe streets and amend the 2026 budget. This would allow the city to receive a federal grant of up to $3,987,536.00 from the U.S. Department of Transportation for safe streets initiatives. It would also appropriate $4,984,420.00 into the Safe Streets for All (Ss4a) Grant Revenue and Expense accounts.
Northwest Arkansas housing market stabilizes. The Northwest Arkansas housing market is now considered a buyer's market for the first time in five years, with prices beginning to stabilize, according to Arvest's first half of 2026 Skyline report. Home sales continue to increase, though pricing was mixed with average prices declining in Benton and Madison counties but still rising in other areas.
Federal judge rules Arkansas ballot measure laws unconstitutional. A federal judge on Friday ruled several Arkansas laws regarding citizen ballot measures are unconstitutional and issued a permanent injunction against their enforcement.
7hills plans to sell day center for affordable housing. 7hills Homeless Center announced its intention to sell its day center in south Fayetteville to a company that plans to develop affordable housing on the site.
Siloam Springs interim police chief Derek Spicer to retire. Interim Siloam Springs Police Chief Derek Spicer announced his retirement, making him the second Siloam Springs police chief to retire this year. His retirement is planned for next month.
Samaritan community center to host job fair. A Northwest Arkansas nonprofit will host a free job fair next week.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
UA cleans up after water leak at reid hall. A water leak in a University of Arkansas residence hall has displaced students until at least Sunday.
Siloam Springs school district launches podcast. The Siloam Springs School District has launched the Panther Pulse Podcast to keep the community informed about district happenings.
Bentonville panel discusses Marshallese community. A Bentonville panel discussed the Marshallese community in Northwest Arkansas, highlighting efforts to raise awareness about why the region has the largest Marshallese population in the country.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 20, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved the overarching site plan for a new university campus.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves walton STEM university plan. The Bentonville Planning Commission unanimously approved the overarching site plan for a new university campus.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and a final recommendation on 'Near the Pitch'. This item involves a public art project that the board will review and potentially recommend for approval, which could lead to its installation in the city.
Bentonville School District increases bus driver pay. The Bentonville School Board voted to increase pay for bus drivers after starting the new school year with a shortage.
Rogers school board approves seven Cambridge international courses. The Rogers School Board approved seven new Cambridge courses for middle and high school students, making the district the first in Arkansas to offer the Cambridge Pathway.
Rogers Animal Services offers fee-waived adoptions. The City of Rogers Animal Services is offering fee-waived adoptions for one year after receiving a $6,000 grant from Best Friends Animal Society.
Fayetteville City Council strengthens data center regulations. The Fayetteville City Council unanimously passed an amendment to strengthen the city's data center regulations.
Lake Sequoyah Drive bridge in Fayetteville to close for rehabilitation. The Lake Sequoyah Drive bridge in Fayetteville will temporarily close for several weeks for a rehabilitation project.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
John Brown University receives $34.5 million for health care master's programs. John Brown University announced a $34.5 million gift commitment to launch four new master's degree tracks in health care.
Arvest Bank CFO Karla Payne to retire in early 2027. Arvest Bank Chief Financial Officer Karla Payne will retire in early 2027 after more than 40 years with the company.
Ozark Quilt Fair returns to Springdale museum. The 48th Annual Ozark Quilt Fair will be held on Saturday, September 12, at the Shiloh Museum grounds in downtown Springdale.
Mercy Fort Smith and NWA recognized for heart attack care. Mercy Hospitals Fort Smith and Mercy Hospitals Northwest Arkansas have been recognized by the American College of Cardiology for their heart attack care.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 19, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved a campus development plan for a business-oriented university focused on STEM.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton County until 9 p.m. Wednesday. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County, effective until 9 p.m. on Wednesday. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 108 degrees.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves Walton STEM university plan. The Bentonville Planning Commission voted 7-0 to approve a campus development plan for a business-oriented university. The university, spearheaded by the Walton family, will focus on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
Bentonville School Board plans evening Star elementary expansion. The Bentonville School Board approved preliminary plans to expand Evening Star Elementary School. This expansion aims to accommodate continued growth in student enrollment.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport Connector Road and Springdale Northern Bypass section to open. The Arkansas Department of Transportation has scheduled a ribbon-cutting for Phase Two of the U.S. 412 Springdale Northern Bypass and the new Connector Road to the Northwest Arkansas National Airport. The opening will provide a quicker route to the airport and Oklahoma.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Public art advisory board to give final recommendation on 'Near the Pitch'. The board would provide feedback and a final recommendation on the 'Near the Pitch' art project.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
Anime Cafe rezoning request on hold due to parking concerns. A rezoning request for the Anime Cafe in Rogers is on hold after the Planning Commission heard concerns about parking. The plan involves putting the cafe on wheels at a proposed new location.
Community Connections expands services into Northwest Arkansas. Conway-based nonprofit Community Connections is expanding its services to Northwest Arkansas. The organization provides support for children with special needs and their families.
Tyson Foods announces plant closures impacting over 3,000 workers. Tyson Foods will close two plants, affecting more than 3,000 workers. The closures are attributed to a 'historic cattle shortage'.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport sets July enplanement record. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) recorded its highest monthly number of enplanements in July. More individuals boarded flights during this month than in any previous month on record.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 18, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory is in effect for Benton County until Wednesday evening, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton county. A Heat Advisory has been issued for Benton County until August 19 at 9:00 PM CDT, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees. The advisory is in effect from 1 PM Tuesday to 9 PM CDT Wednesday, impacting portions of northwest and west central Arkansas and east central and northeast Oklahoma.
Benton County Quorum Court pauses sales tax reallocation vote. The Benton County Quorum Court will not pursue placing a plan to reallocate county sales tax revenue on the November 3 ballot. This decision follows discussions with mayors in the county.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to approve waiving bids for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the Bentonville Utility Board to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax without competitive bidding, due to market volatility and long lead times for these products. These breakers are for future capital projects at substations.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to hold public hearing on rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale commercial uses at 405 NW 5th Street, potentially increasing density and local services in the area.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: The board will consider a proposal for an art piece called 'Old Tree' by Pamela Rosenkranz.. This item would decide whether to move forward with a new public art installation in the city.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on August 18 at 5:30 PM. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, and approval of the agenda.
Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority recommends lawn watering moratorium. The Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority recommends a lawn watering moratorium through September 1. This recommendation comes from the general manager of the authority.
Bentonville Restaurant Week begins. The 2026 Bentonville Restaurant Week began on August 16, featuring new menus, specials, and activities. The event celebrates restaurants and the community across the city.
New AI startups arrive in Bentonville for 10-week program. Startup Junkie Foundation’s Fuel Accelerator will launch its Fall 2026 AI/ML cohort in Bentonville, welcoming 12 artificial intelligence and machine learning ventures. The 10-week program of expert-led curriculum begins on August 25.
Walmart expected to report 7% earnings gain. Walmart is expected to post a 7% earnings gain in its second quarter, according to analysts and economists. The company's second-quarter financial results for the period ending July 31 will be released Thursday morning.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
BIT and HVACr Academy partner for training program. Springdale-based nonprofit Business & Industry Training and Arkansas HVACr Academy have partnered to offer a new heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration technician training program. The program is set to begin in August.
National institutes of Health awards $11.2 million to University of Arkansas center. The National Institutes of Health has awarded $11.2 million in Phase 2 funding to the Arkansas Integrative Metabolic Research Center at the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 17, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will meet on August 18 to approve its agenda and recognize achievements.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on August 18. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on August 18, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, roll call, and approval of the agenda, with recognitions also planned.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to waive competitive bidding for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the Bentonville Utility Board to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, for future substation projects. This decision is proposed due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to hold public hearing on rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale commercial uses at 405 NW 5th Street, potentially increasing density and local services in the area.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This means you would pay less tax when purchasing meals and drinks from local establishments.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and final recommendation on 'Near the Pitch'. This item involves a public art project that the board will review and potentially recommend for approval, which could lead to a new art installation in the city.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place on October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
Kalene Griffith appointed to Destinations International board. Kalene Griffith, who serves as the president and CEO of Visit Bentonville, has been appointed to the board of directors for Destinations International. This organization collaborates with travel and tourism executives to promote destinations.
Pea Ridge development plans move forward despite opposition. Plans for the Village at City Park, a mixed-use development on 10 acres east of Pea Ridge City Park, are progressing. This comes despite public opposition to the project.
Gentry implements new fees for late utility bill payments. Residents utilizing Gentry utilities may now incur penalties and face service disruptions for late bill payments. These new rules have been recently adopted by the city.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 16, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory has been issued for Benton County until 8 PM CDT tonight, with heat index values up to 108 degrees.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton County. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County until 8 PM CDT tonight, with heat index values expected to reach up to 108 degrees.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to approve waiving bids for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the Bentonville Electric Utility Department (BEUD) to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without competitive bidding, for future substation projects.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to hold a public hearing on rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed rezoning would change the allowed uses at 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family homes to a neighborhood node, which typically allows for a mix of residential and commercial uses at a higher density.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%, potentially making dining out slightly less expensive.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and a final recommendation for 'Near the Pitch'. This item involves a public art project, and the board's decision would determine its future development or approval.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on August 18 at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 500 Tiger Blvd.
Lowell buys $5.9 million buildings for city expansion. The City of Lowell has purchased buildings on JB Hunt Corporate Drive for $5.9 million as part of a plan to address overcrowding and expand city facilities.
Northwest Arkansas Land Trust protects 66 acres in War Eagle Creek Watershed. The Northwest Arkansas Land Trust has announced a new conservation agreement to protect a 66-acre forest in Madison County from future development.
Arthur Henderson donates Benton County farm for conservation. Benton County landowner Arthur Henderson is reserving his farm for nature, despite high demand for real estate development in Northwest Arkansas.
Circle of life to acquire Washington Regional Hospice. Springdale-based hospice provider Circle of Life is set to acquire Washington Regional Hospice.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Filipino festival to celebrate culture, cuisine, and tradition. The Filipino American Organization of Northwest Arkansas is hosting its annual Barrio Fiesta to celebrate Filipino American culture, cuisine, and tradition.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 15, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until Saturday evening, with heat index values expected to reach 110 degrees.
NWS tulsa issues heat advisory for Benton county. A heat advisory has been issued for Benton County from August 14 at 10:49 PM CDT until August 16 at 8:00 PM CDT. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 110 degrees on Saturday, with higher values possible on Sunday.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to waive competitive bidding for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the Bentonville Utility Board to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, for future substation projects. This decision is proposed due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale commercial uses at 405 NW 5th Street, potentially increasing density and local services in the area.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This means you would pay less tax when purchasing meals and drinks from local establishments.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and a final recommendation for 'Near the Pitch'. This item involves a public art project that the board will discuss and potentially recommend for approval, which could lead to a new art installation in the city.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on August 18. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on August 18, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, and approval of the agenda.
Circle of Life to purchase Washington Regional Hospice. Springdale-based Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and its Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville. Circle of Life is a nonprofit offering hospice and palliative care.
Walmart recalls tomato soup products due to listeria risk. Walmart stores in several states, including Arkansas, are recalling certain tomato soup products due to potential listeria contamination. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration reported the recall.
Fayetteville to close lane on Mission Boulevard for sidewalk construction. One lane of Mission Boulevard in Fayetteville will experience closures for new sidewalk construction beginning August 17. The closures are expected to last for several months.
Tyson Foods beef plant closures to impact communities. Tyson Foods' closure of two beef processing facilities and exploration of selling a third will create significant challenges and uncertainty in the affected communities. This information comes from beef organizations and local elected officials.
NorthWest Arkansas Community college receives $600,000 grant for mentorship. The Northwest Arkansas Community College's LIFE program has received a nearly $600,000 grant from the Walton Family Foundation. This funding will allow the program to expand its mentorship initiatives.
Fayetteville hosts bike helmet giveaway. The City of Fayetteville is hosting a bike helmet giveaway to promote cycling safety. This initiative aims to ensure residents can enjoy cycling safely.
Fayetteville Mayor Rawn appoints new c-suite members. Fayetteville Mayor Molly Rawn has appointed Jennifer Walker as the city’s chief of staff and Keith Macedo as chief information officer. These appointments are effective immediately.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 14, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory has been issued for Benton County until Sunday at 8:00 PM CDT, with heat index values expected to reach 105 to 110 degrees.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton County. The National Weather Service in Tulsa, Oklahoma, has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County, effective until Sunday, August 16, at 8:00 PM CDT. Heat index values are forecast to be between 105 and 110 degrees.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet August 18. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on August 18, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 500 Tiger Blvd. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, and approval of the agenda.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to hold a public hearing on rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed rezoning would change the allowed uses at 405 NW 5th Street from single-family homes to a neighborhood node, which typically allows for a mix of residential and small-scale commercial uses.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This means you would pay less tax when purchasing meals and drinks from local establishments.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and final recommendation on 'Near the Pitch'. The board will discuss and potentially make a final decision on a public art project or initiative known as 'Near the Pitch'.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to approve Resolution 26-23 for purchasing plan review software. This resolution would authorize the purchase of software to assist with reviewing plans, potentially streamlining development processes related to water and sewer infrastructure.
Michaels to open new concept store in Rogers. Michaels is scheduled to open a new concept store location in Rogers.
Walmart AMP plans new buildings on property. City records indicate that the Walmart AMP concert venue is planning to add additional facilities to its property.
Alice L. Walton School of Medicine grows to nearly 100 students. The Alice L. Walton School of Medicine (AWSOM) in Bentonville has expanded its student body to 96, following the enrollment of its second class of 48 students in July.
NWACC and MIT collaborate on artificial intelligence curriculum. NorthWest Arkansas Community College (NWACC) and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Pathways for AI Training and Hiring program met in Bentonville to explore developing an artificial intelligence curriculum.
Benton County to host annual passport Saturday event. Benton County will host its annual "Passport Saturday" event next month, allowing residents to apply for new passports without needing an appointment.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 13, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory covering Benton County runs through Friday evening, with heat index values expected to reach 109 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County through Friday. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for Benton County and surrounding areas from Wednesday morning through Friday at 8 p.m., with heat index values forecast to reach 109 degrees.
Centerton approves $16.59 million bond for sewer system improvements. Centerton City Council approved a $16.59 million bond issue to fund improvements to the city's sewer collection system, which will allow additional development.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Rezone 405 NW 5th Street from single-family to neighborhood node. The property would shift from low-density suburban residential to a denser neighborhood node classification, allowing for different housing types and more concentrated development.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Propose changes to the Future Land Use Map. The map that guides long-term growth and development could be updated, affecting where different types of housing, businesses, and public uses are allowed across the city.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Update the community Code with ordinance amendments. The changes would revise existing development rules and standards, altering requirements for design, parking, and other site features for properties in the city.
Springdale City Council fills Ward 2 vacancy with former member. The Springdale City Council appointed a former council member to temporarily fill a Ward 2 vacancy for the next few months.
Herman's Ribhouse working to reopen in Fayetteville. Owner Nick Wright said work is underway to reopen the longtime Fayetteville restaurant.
Gentry Public Schools offering free lunches to all students. Starting this school year, Gentry Public Schools is providing lunch to all students at no charge.
Madison County forest gains permanent protection through conservation easement. The Northwest Arkansas Land Trust announced that a forested tract in Madison County will be permanently protected through a conservation easement.
Congressman Womack discusses airport loan application with federal official. Congressman Steve Womack and a U.S. Department of Transportation official met with Northwest Arkansas National Airport CEO Aaron Burkes to discuss the airport's application for a loan to fund a new concourse and rental car parking garage.
Ten tech companies pitch to investors at Fuse Demo Day. Ten Northwest Arkansas tech companies presented emerging technologies to investors, government stakeholders and economic developers at Fuse Ventures' Demo Day.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 12, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory through August 16 is in effect for Benton County as officials highlight water conservation progress across Northwest Arkansas.
Heat Advisory issued through August 16 for Benton County. The National Weather Service has issued a Moderate Heat Advisory covering Benton County and multiple surrounding areas, active until August 13 at 1:15 AM.
Rogers voters to decide on issuing more than $450 million in bonds. Rogers voters will decide in November whether to allow the city to issue more than $450 million in bonds for capital improvement projects.
Centerton removes Flock Safety cameras. Centerton City Council voted to end the town's use of Flock Safety cameras, joining other Arkansas cities in removing the surveillance system.
Citizens Bank to open Fayetteville banking center. Batesville-based The Citizens Bank plans to open a new banking center at 1350 E. Joyce Blvd. in Fayetteville, moving beyond traditional banking models.
Walmart AMP plans two-story addition in Rogers. The Walmart Arkansas Music Pavilion in Rogers is planning a two-story front-of-house addition and a north addition, according to city plans.
Washington Regional hires chief medical informatics officer. Dr. Rowland “Todd” Stewart recently joined Washington Regional as vice president and the Fayetteville-based health system’s first chief medical informatics officer.
World champion squirrel cook off returns to Springdale. Hunters, outdoor enthusiasts and curious food lovers will converge on Springdale next month for a celebration of squirrel cooking.
Arkansas sees dip in new cyclosporiasis cases. The Arkansas Department of Health has identified 15 new cases of cyclosporiasis in a three-day span, more than half of which were in Northwest Arkansas.
Swarm Aero awarded $10 million government contract. Unmanned aircraft-maker Swarm Aero has secured a $10 million government contract that will be primarily executed at its new Fayetteville research and manufacturing facility.
Bentonville to close portion of southeast a street. The city is warning motorists to be aware of a street closing set to begin Thursday for water line work.
Two buildings demolished on college avenue in Fayetteville. Two buildings on one of Fayetteville's busiest streets have been razed to make way for a new bank.
Water conservation efforts show progress across NWA. After one day of suggested water savings, Scott Borman of the Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority reported a noticeable difference in usage across the community.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 11, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory is in effect for Benton County with heat index values up to 109 expected until 8:00 PM this evening.
Heat Advisory in effect until 8:00 PM this evening. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County and surrounding areas due to heat index values reaching up to 109 degrees. The advisory is in effect until 8:00 PM CDT.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for properties at 902, 904, 906, 908, and 1002 SE 3rd Street. If approved, the specified properties would be developed under a Planned Unit Development, allowing a particular mixed-use design as outlined in the submitted plan.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Authorization to accept grant for adaptive traffic signals. The council would approve taking a $700,000 grant to test AI-based traffic signals that adjust timing in real time, with a budget change needed to record and spend the grant money.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Proposed changes to the Future Land Use Map. Adopting the map changes would guide where different types of development are allowed across the city for years to come.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 10, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory will affect Benton County through 8 p.m. today, with heat index values expected to reach 109 degrees.
Heat advisory in effect for Benton County through this evening. The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory for Benton County and surrounding areas through 8 p.m. today, with heat index values expected to reach 109 degrees.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for properties at 902, 904, 906, 908, and 1002 SE 3rd Street. If approved, the detailed development plan for these parcels would be finalized, guiding how the site is built and used.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Accept a grant to test adaptive traffic signals.. The city would receive a $700,000 grant to evaluate adaptive AI-based traffic signal technologies, leading to potential changes in how traffic lights operate in some areas.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Vacate a right of way and establish a drainage easement at Lot 13, Block 11 and Block 14 of Gilmore's Addition. The action would formally vacate the street right of way and create a drainage easement, affecting access and stormwater management for the area.
Bentonville council to consider items at Tuesday meetings. The Bentonville Finance Committee meets at 5 p.m. Tuesday, followed by a Combined Committee of the Whole and City Council meeting at 6 p.m. Agendas are available on the city portal.
Bella Vista holds short-term rental cap at 600 units. Following three months of City Council discussion, Bella Vista is maintaining its limit of 600 allowed short-term rentals after strong opposition to raising the number.
Rogers approves tree canopy restoration from 2024 tornado. Rogers City Council approved efforts to restore the city's tree canopy damaged in the 2024 tornado.
Samaritan Community Center names Gardner Andreas as executive director. Samaritan Community Center announced Gardner Andreas as its new executive director, with former executive director Debbie Rambo transitioning to a new role.
Swarm Aero receives $10 million in Air Force contracts. Swarm Aero, a drone company with manufacturing operations in Fayetteville, received $10 million in federal contracts to advance its high-rate manufacturing technology and produce aircraft components.
Flyway Brewing Company opens at Walmart Home Office. Flyway Brewing Company, a Little Rock-based microbrewery, officially opened Monday at Walmart's Home Office.
J.B. Hunt marks 65 years in business. J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. celebrated its 65th anniversary Monday by ringing the Nasdaq opening bell.
NWACC launches new dining service in student center. Northwest Arkansas Community College is launching a new on-campus dining service this week as students and staff return for the new semester.
Fayetteville schools, police urge caution as students return to class. Fayetteville Public Schools begin Tuesday, and police are urging all drivers in the city to slow down and pay closer attention as students return to class.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 9, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 8 p.m. Sunday, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County through Sunday evening. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for Benton County from noon to 8 p.m. CDT on Sunday, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees. Heat-related illnesses are possible, especially for those not acclimated to the conditions.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for 1002 SE 3rd Street. The council would approve a PUD that allows more dense, mixed-use development at this corner, changing what can be built there.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Authorization to accept grant for adaptive traffic signals. The council would approve taking a $700,000 grant to evaluate AI-based traffic signal technologies that could change how traffic is managed in the city.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Vacate a Right of Way and create a Drainage Easement at Gilmore's Addition. The ordinance would close this street segment and allow stormwater drainage infrastructure, affecting access and flooding management for nearby properties.
Bentonville council to consider finance and other matters at Monday meetings. The Bentonville Finance Committee meets Monday at 5 p.m., followed by a combined Committee of the Whole and City Council meeting at 6 p.m. Agendas have been published for both meetings.
Taziki's opens Rogers location. Taziki's Mediterranean Café opened at 1771 W. Pleasant Grove Road, Suite 104, in Rogers. The approximately 2,900-square-foot restaurant seats 85 guests and required $950,000 in investment.
Simmons Foods promotes Scott Salmon to chief commercial officer. Siloam Springs-based Simmons Foods promoted Scott Salmon, president of Simmons Pet Food, to the newly created role of chief commercial officer. Jacob Rogers will succeed Salmon in his previous position.
Walton Family Foundation grants $599,139 to NWACC for LIFE program. The Walton Family Foundation provided a $599,139 grant to Northwest Arkansas Community College to expand its Learning, Improvement, Fun and Empowerment program.
Jessica DeBari named executive director of Community Creative Center. Fayetteville artist Jessica DeBari has been appointed executive director of Community Creative Center, a Fayetteville-based nonprofit arts organization. She replaces Bryce Brisco, who stepped down in late July.
Tyson Foods board declares quarterly dividend of 51 cents per share. The Tyson Foods board of directors declared a quarterly dividend payment of 51 cents per share for Class A shareholders, payable on December 15.
Downtown Springdale Alliance hosts free picnic in the park series. Throughout August, the Downtown Springdale Alliance is hosting weekly Saturday events featuring food, music, and community gathering.
Terra Studios to host fourth annual Paws, Paint, & Play event in September. Terra Studios will host its fourth annual Paws, Paint, & Play event, a canine-friendly art park experience, on Sunday, September 6 from noon to 4 p.m.
Benton County study identifies site as candidate for possible nuclear development. A study presented to Arkansas lawmakers identified a site in Benton County as a candidate for possible future nuclear power development.
Benton County holds meeting on one-cent sales tax proposal. Benton County held an intergovernmental meeting to discuss a proposed one-cent sales tax.
